messages.content:
Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Adults with depressive symptoms had lower serum 25(OH)D than those without.
Sentence: "Subjects with depressive symptoms had lower serum levels of 25(OH)D (41.6±16.2 nmol/L) than those without (44.3±16.2 nmol/L; P-value<0.05; effect size = 0.17)."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (answering yes on a depressive symptoms question)
Population: Korean adults aged 20 and older from KNHANES V-1 2010
Intervention: Serum 25(OH)D level (observational, not given)
Comparator: Subjects without depressive symptoms / higher 25(OH)D
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 3,570
baseline_vitamin_d_status: below_20_ng_ml

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: In the RCT, vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood, including depression.
Sentence: "The vitamin C supplementation did not affect mood and serum concentrations of BDNF."
Measured as: depression (mood status)
Population: Healthy subjects with inadequate serum vitamin C (<50 μmol/L), n = 46
Intervention: Vitamin C 500 mg twice a day for 4 weeks
Comparator: Placebo
Design: randomized controlled trial
Sample size: 260
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Responses

content.text: {"evaluation":"All three responses correctly identify that Study B tests vitamin C, not vitamin D, so the pair is off_question with no reason and no also_differs. They differ only in the specificity of the detail field and in using a 'rationale' key instead of the schema's 'evaluation' key (all share this flaw). Response B's detail adds dose and duration, A's adds dose and attribution to Study B, and C's is the most generic but still accurate.","ranking":["B","A","C"]}
